part.text:
Fixed the nested-fallback regression with `merge()` in two places:

- `axum/src/routing/mod.rs:237` (`Router::merge`): instead of wholesale replacing `self.fallback_router` with the other router's (which discarded nested fallback endpoints), all cases now merge the fallback routers via `PathRouter::merge`. When self has a custom fallback and other has the default, the merge is done in the other direction so other's default top-level fallbacks win.
- `axum/src/routing/path_router.rs:114` (`PathRouter::merge`): when merging into a fallback router, top-level fallback endpoints (`/` and `/*__private__axum_fallback`) are installed via `replace_endpoint` (avoiding route conflicts) while nested fallback paths go through the normal `route`/`route_service` path, preserving them. Also introduced a shared `FALLBACK_PARAM_PATH` constant.

Verification: all 21 `routing::tests::fallback` tests pass (including the FAIL_TO_PASS cases `issue_2072*`, `merge_router_with_fallback_into_nested_router_with_fallback`, etc.), the full `cargo test -p axum` suite passes except `logging_rejections`, which I confirmed fails on the pristine tree too (pre-existing, environment-related). A temporary integration test replicating the exact issue snippet (nested router with fallback + merge of a routed router, with and without an outer fallback) passed and was removed afterward.
